project.name: @kehto/mocks
project.summary: Pretend versions of every napplet NAP domain (relays, files, devices, AI, downloads and more) that keep all their data in memory and behave the same way every run. A shell that hosts napplets (small sandboxed web apps) can plug them in to get realistic answers while it builds support for a NAP, without real relays, devices or providers. Each pretend service records the exact napplet/naps spec version it follows, and a script reports when the spec has moved on.

nodes.label: Front door
nodes.summary: What shells import: the full list of NAP domains with their spec versions, and one call that builds a ready-made environment of every pretend service with a shared Nostr store and saved-data store.

nodes.label: Mock building kit
nodes.summary: The shared machinery every pretend service is built from: matching incoming messages to answers, recording everything sent back, repeatable random ids and keys, a controllable clock and delays, and bundling many services into one set.

nodes.label: NAP domain mocks
nodes.summary: One pretend service per NAP domain, each answering that domain's messages from seeded in-memory data and exposing controls to inspect, reset or drive it.

nodes.label: Nostr social
nodes.summary: Relays, outbox routing, counts, profiles, keys, direct messages, lists, shared Nostr helpers, proof-of-work and payments, mostly reading and writing one shared store of Nostr events.

nodes.label: Files and storage
nodes.summary: Napplet file system, saved settings, Blossom and Hashtree file hosting, uploads, fetched resources and Git repositories, all held as bytes in memory.

nodes.label: Downloads and peer links
nodes.summary: Torrent, Usenet (NZB) and Soulseek downloads that progress on a pretend timeline, plus peer-to-peer WebRTC connections.

nodes.label: Devices and sensors
nodes.summary: Bluetooth, serial ports, game controllers, motion, location, camera capture, media playback and displays, with controls to simulate presses, readings and device events.

nodes.label: Shell and app frame
nodes.summary: Domains about the hosting shell itself: theme, navigation, notifications, intents and the installed-napplet catalog, links, system info, settings, background workers, security class and network grants, plus registry-only entries for the parts the runtime handles itself (shell, inter-napplet messages).

nodes.label: AI and remote tools
nodes.summary: A pretend language-model provider with canned answers and request checks, and pretend ContextVM servers offering remote tools and resources.

nodes.label: Sample data
nodes.summary: Fixed sample accounts, Nostr events and relays, Linux distribution images and example web addresses that the pretend services seed themselves with.

nodes.label: Spec audit and build tools
nodes.summary: Command-line tools that compare each mock's recorded spec version with the live napplet/naps repository, keep a list of drafts deliberately not mocked yet, and regenerate the domain table in the docs, plus the package's build settings.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.summary: Automatic checks for every domain mock, the building kit, the registry and environment, the sample data, retired names and the audit script.

nodes.label: Kehto runtime
nodes.summary: The kehto protocol engine whose service interface every mock implements and which delivers messages to them.

nodes.label: Napplet protocol types
nodes.summary: The published napplet core and NAP packages that define each domain's message shapes.

nodes.label: napplet/naps on GitHub
nodes.summary: The spec repository (master plus open pull requests) the audit script reads through the GitHub command-line tool.

Once a shell registers a mock, the runtime hands it each napplet message for its domain.

flows.title: A shell gets a full set of pretend services

steps.note: The shell calls the environment builder, optionally with a seed and a list of domains.
The registry reads every domain's entry: its spec version, kind and factory.
Each factory is called with shared options, giving a domain-to-service map.
The social domains share one seeded Nostr event store so they see the same events.
That store starts from fixed sample accounts and events.

flows.title: A napplet asks a mock something

steps.note: The runtime receives a message from a napplet and hands it to the registered mock for that domain.
The domain mock looks up the route for that exact message type and works out the answer from its in-memory state.
The kit records the reply and pushes it back to the napplet's window, after any configured delay.
Reads the spec ref each domain module records and the deferred list.
Fetches current document heads from napplet/naps master and open pull requests.
After a rebuild, rewrites the domain table in the README and docs page.

tour.title: What this package is
tour.note: Pretend NAP services a shell can plug in to have data before the real thing exists. Start with the registry and environment builder.

tour.title: How every mock is built
tour.note: All mocks share one recipe: a table of message types to answers, plus controls to inspect state, reset it and see what was sent.

tour.title: One mock per NAP
tour.note: Grouped here by area: social, files, downloads, devices, shell, and AI.

tour.title: Repeatable sample data
tour.note: Fixed accounts, events and files so every run gives the same answers.

tour.title: Keeping up with the specs
tour.note: The audit tool flags any mock whose recorded spec version no longer matches napplet/naps.
